_comment: Well-established facts the bot checks the child's statements against (services/response_engine.py, _fact_reply). A statement that matches a fact's form and gets it wrong ("spiders have 6 legs") is disputed with the "wrong" replies; one that gets it right is confirmed with the "right" replies; {correct} is the fact's "correct" text. Patterns are regular expressions matched against the whole statement, lowercased, without punctuation or apostrophes, after openers like "no" or "I think". Types: "count" ("<subject> have <number> <noun>", value a number or a list of accepted numbers), "there_are" ("there are <number> <noun>"), "is" ("<subject> is/are <x>": x in "true" is right, in "false" is wrong; "isn't" turns them around) and "can" ("<subject> can <verb>", value true or false). An "is" fact's "false_from" names lists in "sets" whose other values are wrong too (any capital but Paris for France), and an "is" statement is also read the other way around ("venus is the hottest planet"). A fact can give its own "wrong" replies. "examples" pairs a statement with "wrong", "right" or null (not checked); tests/test_facts.py checks them. "facts" are written by hand; "sets" and "generated" are made by scripts/build_facts.py from its tables (run it after changing them, not edit them here). Only add facts that are simply true for a child, without exceptions worth arguing about.

wrong: Hmm, I don't think that's right! {correct}
insist: I'm pretty sure about this one! {correct} You could check in a book or ask a grown-up to be sure.
Hmm, I still think so! {correct} Want to look it up with a grown-up to check?
